title: Exceptions under M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 4 and the conditions and record book for dispensing or selling excepted preparations under s. 5
rule_summary: Under M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 4, the commissioner acting jointly with the board of registration in pharmacy may by regulation pursuant to chapter 30A except any compound, mixture or preparation containing any substances in paragraph (a) or (b) of Schedule III or in Schedule IV, V or VI from the application of all or any part of chapter 94C if (1) the compound, mixture, or preparation contains one or more active medicinal ingredients not having a depressant or stimulant effect on the central nervous system, (2) such ingredients are included therein in such combinations, quantity, proportion, or concentration as to vitiate the potential for abuse of the substances which do have a depressant or stimulant effect on the central nervous system, and (3) the compound, mixture, or preparation has been similarly excepted under the federal Comprehensive Drug Abuse Prevention and Control Act of 1970 or any amendment of it. Such a regulation shall state the weight of the controlled substance per fluid ounce, or if a solid or semi-solid preparation the weight in the avoirdupois amounts, and if the metric system is used, the weight in grams per hundred cubic centimeters for a fluid or the weight per gram for a solid or semi-solid preparation, and the commissioner shall by regulation modify, rescind or revoke an exception whenever it has been modified, rescinded or revoked under the federal Act. Under s. 5, controlled substances which are excepted pursuant to s. 4 may be dispensed, or sold at retail, subject to the conditions (1) that the preparation is dispensed, or sold in good faith as a medicine, and not for the purpose of evading the provisions of the controlled substances law; (2) that the purchaser of the preparation identify himself to the satisfaction of the pharmacist; and (3) that not more than four ounces of the preparation are dispensed, or sold to a person during any 48 hour period; and the pharmacist dispensing such excepted substances shall keep an accurate record book including the name and address of the purchaser, the name of the preparation, the strength per dosage unit, the quantity dispensed and the date. Section 1 of chapter 94C defines pharmacist as any pharmacist registered in the commonwealth to dispense controlled substances, and including any other person authorized to dispense controlled substances under the supervision of a pharmacist registered in the commonwealth. No other section of chapter 94C refers to a controlled substance being sold at retail. 105 CMR 700.002 establishes Schedules I through V as the drugs and other substances listed in 21 CFR 1308.11 through 1308.15 and Schedule VI as all prescription drugs not included in any other schedule, and neither 105 CMR 700.000 nor 247 CMR 2.00 through 21.00 states an exception under s. 4.
exam_relevance: Tests that the s. 5 route is available only for a preparation actually excepted by regulation under s. 4, and the s. 5 terms: good faith as a medicine, identification to the pharmacist's satisfaction, not more than four ounces to a person during any 48 hour period, and the record book's five items.

exceptions: A regulation under s. 4 may except a preparation from the application of all or any part of chapter 94C.
common_confusions: A preparation's placement in Schedule V, or its federal marketing as a nonprescription drug, is not an exception under s. 4; the exception is made by regulation of the commissioner acting jointly with the Board.
Section 5 states no minimum age for the purchaser.
The four-ounce ceiling applies per person during any 48 hour period, not per transaction or per calendar day.
The s. 5 record book includes the strength per dosage unit, an item the federal bound record book under 21 CFR 1306.26 does not list.
